title: Pin VMware guest outputs to the host monitor layout
head: 25cfdfd1c0d0

leads.summary: The first hotplug after daemon startup, or a hotplug during monitor restart, can be lost
leads.consequence: Initial sync_layout runs before udevadm monitor is even started. If the host changes layout after that sync read but before the udev subscription starts, the kernel emits its one DRM hotplug while nobody is listening. No further sync happens until the next host push, so monitor mode/position may remain stale, including the inaccessible-pointer case this PR fixes. The two-second pause after a dead udevadm produces a similar gap. Subscribe first, then do a full initial sync; resync immediately after each subscription restart.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral SendMessage to Opus; confirmed and reproduced (opus/followup-sync-window.md); published in More findings as F4

leads.summary: A same-named Virtual connector on another DRM card supplies the VMware output's wrong mode
leads.consequence: modetest selects vmwgfx, but the subsequent global sysfs glob picks the first card*-Virtual-1/modes, not necessarily the vmwgfx card. On a guest with another virtual DRM device enumerated earlier, for example a virtio-gpu Virtual-1, the helper emits vmwgfx's host offset with the other card's size. A wrong named hl.monitor rule then persists on load and resync, potentially defeating the host layout and pointer alignment. Link modetest's selected DRM card to its sysfs connector or check the candidate card's driver before reading its modes.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (noted harmless on normal VMware guest); not published

leads.summary: Open PR #7000's monitor-management off toggle does not stop this PR's VMware automatic monitor writer
leads.consequence: #7000 explicitly promises that toggling monitor-management off lets an external manager take ownership of monitor layout, and guards all its existing automatic writers. This PR's new VMware module and udev daemon check only the separate omarchy_vmware_layout opt-out and VMware hardware; they keep re-pinning host offsets/modes on reload and every host hotplug even while management is off. An external monitor manager will fight these rules in VMware guests, despite the off setting, with potentially inaccessible monitors. Make the VMware writer honor the shared ownership toggle in config load and on each sync when #7000 lands, or clearly scope the toggle contract and document how external managers opt out of VMware pinning.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** VMware outputs are pinned at scale 1; only turning the layout feature off lets another scale stick.

### VMware outputs are held at 1x while the layout is managed

`default/hypr/vmware.lua` pins every output with a named `hl.monitor` rule at `scale = 1` on every reload and host push. Named rules beat the `monitors.lua` catch-all, so its scale, a user's own `Virtual-N` scale and Super + / never stick. **Impact:** on a HiDPI host the desktop stays at 1x unless `omarchy_vmware_layout = false`, which also drops the layout fix; this includes integer scales, although #11911 says `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling` keeps working. Verified from Hyprland 0.56.2 source, not on a guest.

**Suggested change:** Add a scale setting for the pins (for example `omarchy_vmware_scale`, default 1, with host offsets divided by it), or at least document the 1x hold in `manual/49-omarchy-on.md`.

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

**A reload turns on displays the lock screen turned off.** `screens_are_off()` takes any output with `dpms_status == false` for an interrupted blink, so the `config.reloaded` handler schedules the 250/1200/2500 ms "on" retries. A reload while the lock screen has blanked the displays therefore turns them back on; the known limitations list only the push case. Suggested change: mark an in-flight blink outside the Lua state (for example a file under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) and re-arm only when it is present.

**A reload applies the catch-all before the pins.** The comment above `config.reloaded` says the pins land before Hyprland applies rules on every reload. In Hyprland 0.56.2, `postConfigReload` runs `ensureMonitorStatus()` before emitting `config.reloaded` on non-first launches, so each reload first applies the catch-all to every VMware output (left to right, with the stale preferred mode after a resize) and then the pins, committing each output twice; the final state is correct. Verified from source, not reproduced. Suggested change: also call `pin(layout, names)` at config load, right after `local names = sorted_names(layout)`, keeping the `config.reloaded` pass. The test "config load writes no rules before config.reloaded" would need updating. Wording: in the comment above `pin()`, it is the pin that merges over a user's own rule, not the other way round.

**A push just before udevadm listens is missed until the next push or reload.** `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-vmware-sync` resyncs once, then starts `udevadm monitor`, which receives only live events. A push after that resync reads the layout but before udevadm binds, or during the 2 s restart pause (only if udevadm dies while the compositor runs, which is rare), gets no resync until the next push or config reload. The window is narrow (tens of milliseconds at startup, by estimate), but a missed single-screen move is the PR's own no-cursor case. Suggested change: resync when udevadm prints its `UDEV - ` banner (printed after it binds) instead of once before the loop.

**From the #11911 commits:**
- Open #10707 adds the same `install/hardware/vmware.sh` and `test/shell.d/vmware-guest-test.sh`, another `open-vm-tools` package line and `run_logged` entry, and its own guest-tools migration. Whichever lands second hits add/add conflicts in those two files, while the package line and `run_logged` entry merge into duplicates, so one of the two needs picking.
- `install/user/all.sh` conflicts with current `quattro` (#13550 added `vm-no-animations.sh` on the same line) and with open #12252. Keeping both lines resolves it; with that resolution, the VMware tests pass on the merge with `quattro`.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: a reload turns on blanked displays (fails at 25cfdfd1)</summary>

Append to `test/shell.d/hyprland-vmware-layout-test.sh` (uses that file's mock and helpers) and run `bash test/shell.d/hyprland-vmware-layout-test.sh`:

```bash
run_scenario "a reload while the lock screen has the displays off" <<'LUA'
set_layout("Virtual-1 0 0 1920x1080\nVirtual-2 1920 0 1920x1080\n")
load_config()
fire("config.reloaded")
-- No push, no blink: the lock screen turned both outputs off, then a reload happened.
monitors = { { name = "Virtual-1", dpms_status = false }, { name = "Virtual-2", dpms_status = false } }
load_config()
fire("config.reloaded")
run_timers()
check_equal(dpms_calls("enable"), "", "a reload leaves displays that the lock screen turned off alone")
LUA
```

Actual output (tail of stderr), exit 1:

```
expected: 
actual:   Virtual-1 Virtual-2 Virtual-1 Virtual-2 Virtual-1 Virtual-2
not ok - a reload leaves displays that the lock screen turned off alone
not ok - a reload while the lock screen has the displays off
```
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: a push before udevadm listens is missed (fails at 25cfdfd1; stubs force the timing)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/hyprland-monitor-vmware-sync-window-test.sh` and run it with `bash`. The stub `udevadm` prints its banner once listening and then only events broadcast after that, as the real one does.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

require_command python3

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

fake_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
runtime_dir="$test_tmp/runtime"
instance_dir="$runtime_dir/hypr/test-instance"
mkdir -p "$fake_bin" "$instance_dir"

# The layout vmwgfx currently holds, and the uevents it has broadcast, one per
# line. A push rewrites the layout, then broadcasts, the order
# vmw_du_update_layout() uses.
kernel_layout="$test_tmp/kernel-layout"
events="$test_tmp/events"
reads="$test_tmp/reads"
udevadm_runs="$test_tmp/udevadm-runs"
hyprctl_calls="$test_tmp/hyprctl-calls"

cat >"$fake_bin/omarchy-hw-vmware" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
SH

cat >"$fake_bin/push" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$1" >"$TEST_KERNEL_LAYOUT"
printf 'UDEV  [1000.000001] change   /devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:0f.0/drm/card0 (drm)\n' >>"$TEST_EVENTS"
SH

# hyprctl eval 'o.vmware_layout.sync()' reads the kernel layout. In the
# startup case the host pushes right after that read, while the daemon is
# still on its way to starting udevadm.
cat >"$fake_bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$TEST_HYPRCTL_CALLS"
cat "$TEST_KERNEL_LAYOUT" >>"$TEST_READS"
if [[ $TEST_CASE == startup && $(grep -c . "$TEST_HYPRCTL_CALLS") == 1 ]]; then
  push "Virtual-1 3840 0 1920x1080"
fi
SH

# udevadm monitor joins the netlink group, then prints its banner, then
# prints each event broadcast from then on; nothing sent before it joined is
# replayed. Each run stays up for a while, then ends; the run that ends the
# test takes the compositor's socket with it.
cat >"$fake_bin/udevadm" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$TEST_UDEVADM_RUNS"
run=$(grep -c . "$TEST_UDEVADM_RUNS")
last_run=2
if [[ $TEST_CASE == startup && $run == 2 ]]; then
  rm -f "$TEST_SOCKET"
  exit 0
fi
seen=$(grep -c . "$TEST_EVENTS")
printf 'monitor will print the received events for:\n'
printf 'UDEV - the event which udev sends out after rule processing\n'
printf '\n'
window=15
[[ $TEST_CASE == restart && $run == 1 ]] && window=5
for (( tick = 0; tick < window; tick++ )); do
  sleep 0.1
  total=$(grep -c . "$TEST_EVENTS")
  while (( seen < total )); do
    seen=$((seen + 1))
    sed -n "${seen}p" "$TEST_EVENTS"
  done
done
(( run >= last_run )) && rm -f "$TEST_SOCKET"
exit 0
SH

# The restart case: the host pushes while udevadm is down, in the pause
# before the daemon starts it again.
cat >"$fake_bin/logger" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
if [[ $TEST_CASE == restart ]]; then
  push "Virtual-1 3840 0 1920x1080"
fi
SH

chmod +x "$fake_bin"/*

run_case() {
  local case_name="$1"

  printf '%s\n' "Virtual-1 0 0 1920x1080" >"$kernel_layout"
  : >"$events"
  : >"$reads"
  : >"$udevadm_runs"
  : >"$hyprctl_calls"
  rm -f "$instance_dir/.socket.sock"
  python3 -c 'import socket,sys; socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX).bind(sys.argv[1])' "$instance_dir/.socket.sock"

  PATH="$fake_bin:$PATH" \
  TEST_CASE="$case_name" \
  TEST_KERNEL_LAYOUT="$kernel_layout" \
  TEST_EVENTS="$events" \
  TEST_READS="$reads" \
  TEST_UDEVADM_RUNS="$udevadm_runs" \
  TEST_HYPRCTL_CALLS="$hyprctl_calls" \
  TEST_SOCKET="$instance_dir/.socket.sock" \
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$runtime_dir" \
  HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE=test-instance \
    timeout 20 "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-vmware-sync" || true
}

# A push that lands after the first resync has read the layout but before
# udevadm is listening.
run_case startup
[[ $(tail -n 1 "$reads") == "$(<"$kernel_layout")" ]] ||
  fail "a push between the first resync and udevadm starting is resynced" \
    "kernel: $(<"$kernel_layout"); last read: $(tail -n 1 "$reads"); resyncs: $(grep -c . "$hyprctl_calls")"
pass "a push between the first resync and udevadm starting is resynced"

# A push that lands while udevadm is being restarted.
run_case restart
[[ $(tail -n 1 "$reads") == "$(<"$kernel_layout")" ]] ||
  fail "a push while udevadm is restarted is resynced" \
    "kernel: $(<"$kernel_layout"); last read: $(tail -n 1 "$reads"); resyncs: $(grep -c . "$hyprctl_calls")"
pass "a push while udevadm is restarted is resynced"
```

Actual output (the file stops at its first failing case), exit 1:

```
kernel: Virtual-1 3840 0 1920x1080; last read: Virtual-1 0 0 1920x1080; resyncs: 1
not ok - a push between the first resync and udevadm starting is resynced
```

The restart case run on its own (startup case removed), exit 1:

```
kernel: Virtual-1 3840 0 1920x1080; last read: Virtual-1 0 0 1920x1080; resyncs: 1
not ok - a push while udevadm is restarted is resynced
```

With this change to `bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-vmware-sync`, both cases pass and the PR's existing sync test still passes:

```diff
@@ -33,13 +33,18 @@
 
 # The config pinned the layout it read when it loaded; anything pushed since
 # is caught here.
-sync_layout
-
 # udevadm monitor is meant to run for the whole session. If it ends anyway,
 # say so and start it again while the compositor is still there, rather than
 # leaving the rest of the session without resyncs.
 while true; do
   while read -r event; do
+    # udevadm prints this once it is listening. Resync then, so a push that
+    # landed before it could hear it, at start or while it was restarted, is
+    # not lost.
+    if [[ $event == "UDEV - "* ]]; then
+      sync_layout
+      continue
+    fi
     [[ $event =~ ^UDEV[[:space:]]+\[ ]] || continue
     settle
     sync_layout
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- All PR tests pass at 25cfdfd1 and on the head merged into current `quattro`; the full shell suite shows the same 7 failures, in files the PR does not touch, at base and head.
- `hl.dsp.dpms({ action, monitor })`, `hl.get_monitors()` fields (`name`, `dpms_status`, nil on an expired handle), `hl.timer` options and the named-rule precedence match Hyprland 0.56.2.
- The helper's parsing matches libdrm 2.4.134 `modetest` output, and the daemon's filter matches `udevadm monitor` output.
- 13 of 15 production mutants fail the PR's tests.

**Optional test improvement:** the two surviving mutants delete the helper's name check (`bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-vmware-layout`, `[[ $name =~ ... ]]`) and its offset check. The injection test still passes because neither hostile name has a sysfs `modes` file, so the mode check skips them first. A case that gives the hostile name a `modes` file fails when the name check is removed; a similar case with a non-numeric suggested offset would cover the offset check.
</details>
